def safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a plain, non-empty file name: no path separators
    (`/` or `\\`), no NUL character, and not `.` or `..`."""
    ex safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex safe_name("") == False
    ex safe_name("..") == False
    ex safe_name(".") == False
    ex safe_name("../secret") == False
    ex safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex safe_name("sub/a.txt") == False
    ex safe_name("a\\b") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    for c in name.chars():
        if c == "/" or c == "\\" or c == "\0":
            return False
    return True

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first name in names that is a safe name (see safe_name) and
    can be read from the directory `notes`, or "" when none can. Unsafe names
    are skipped without touching the file system. Missing or unreadable files
    are skipped. All reads happen inside `with fs = fs.sub("notes"):`, so no
    file outside `notes` is reachable."""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for name in names:
            if not safe_name(name):
                continue
            text = fs.read_text(name) else continue
            return text
    return ""
